item.title: The cart's API
item.description:
The bodies

Start the endpoint package with what the API reads and writes. Its tags become the document’s schemas:

type Cart struct {
	CartID uuid.UUID `json:"cartId" required:"true" format:"uuid"`
	Items []CartItem `json:"items" required:"true"`
	CreatedAt time.Time `json:"createdAt" required:"true"`
	UpdatedAt time.Time `json:"updatedAt" required:"true"`
}

type CartItem struct {
	ItemID uuid.UUID `json:"itemId" required:"true" format:"uuid"`
	CartID uuid.UUID `json:"cartId" required:"true" format:"uuid"`
	ProductID string `json:"productId" required:"true"`
	Quantity int `json:"quantity" required:"true" minimum:"1"`
	UnitPrice float64 `json:"unitPrice" required:"true" minimum:"0"`
	CreatedAt time.Time `json:"createdAt" required:"true"`
	UpdatedAt time.Time `json:"updatedAt" required:"true"`
}

type AddItemRequest struct {
	ProductID string `json:"productId" required:"true" minLength:"1"`
	Quantity int `json:"quantity" required:"true" minimum:"1"`
}

type UpdateItemRequest struct {
	Quantity int `json:"quantity" required:"true" minimum:"1"`
}

An item’s request has no price. The price comes from the catalog, so a client can’t set its own.

item.title: Who may do what
item.description:
Every operation needs a JWT bearer token from the identity provider. Changing a cart needs the scope carts:write too, and a cart is only ever its owner’s.

The claims

The claims the cart reads from a token are a type of its own. HasScope is what auth.RequireScopes asks:

const ScopeWrite = "carts:write"

type Claims struct {
	Subject string `json:"sub"`
	Scope string `json:"scope"`
}

func (c Claims) HasScope(scope string) bool {
	return slices.Contains(strings.Fields(c.Scope), scope)
}

Verifying tokens

Init builds an httpclient client for the key set’s origin, a jwt.RemoteKeySet that fetches the key set with it, and a Verifier of Claims:

item.title: The schema
item.description:
Each service’s schema is a directory of versioned SQL migrations, applied before the service starts by migrate, as a role that owns the schema. The services connect as roles that can only read and write.

The migrations

The cart’s first migration, database/migrations/001_create_carts.sql:

CREATE TABLE carts (
 id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
 owner TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (owner <> ''),
 created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
 updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE cart_items (
 id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
 cart_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES carts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
 product_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
 quantity INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (quantity > 0),
 unit_price DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL CHECK (unit_price >= 0),
 created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
 updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_cart_items_cart_id ON cart_items(cart_id);

The catalog’s, catalog/database/migrations/001_create_products.sql:

item.title: The catalog
item.description:
The catalog is a second humus service, written as the cart is: an openapi/v3 API served by httpserver, on a PostgreSQL database of its own. It has two operations:

  • GET /products/{productId} answers a product and its price, to a caller with a client certificate the internal CA issued, which is the cart;
  • PUT /products/{productId} creates or replaces one, for a bearer token with catalog:write.

The bodies and the Store

type Product struct {
	ProductID string `json:"productId" required:"true"`
	UnitPrice float64 `json:"unitPrice" required:"true" minimum:"0" maximum:"99999999.99"`
}

type PutProductRequest struct {
	UnitPrice *float64 `json:"unitPrice" required:"true" nullable:"false" minimum:"0" maximum:"99999999.99"`
}

const maxUnitPrice = 99999999.99

type Store interface {
	GetProduct(ctx context.Context, productID string) (Product, error)
	PutProduct(ctx context.Context, product Product) (Product, error)
}

var (
	ErrProductNotFound = errors.New("product not found")
	ErrUnavailable = errors.New("the database is unavailable")
)

The maximum is what the table’s DECIMAL(10, 2) holds.

item.title: Calling the catalog
item.description:
The cart has one httpclient client for the catalog. Prices and readiness both go through it.

The client’s settings

The cart’s readSettings starts from httpclient.DefaultSettings(), and sets the catalog’s URL, the CA it trusts the catalog through, and the client certificate it presents:

catalog := httpclient.DefaultSettings()
catalog.BaseURL = r.Get(env("CATALOG_URL").Parse(url.Parse).Validate(checkCatalogURL))
catalog.TLS = &tls.Config{
	RootCAs: r.Get(file("CATALOG_CA_FILE").Parse(certPool)),
	GetClientCertificate: r.Get(env("CATALOG_CLIENT_CERT_FILE").Validate(holdsCertificate(s.Host.FS)).FlatMap(func(certFile string) config.Value[clientCertificate] {
		return env("CATALOG_CLIENT_KEY_FILE").Parse(func(keyFile string) (clientCertificate, error) {
			cfg, err := certfile.Config(s.Host.FS, certFile, keyFile)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			return cfg.GetClientCertificate, nil
		})
	})),
}
catalog.Timeout = r.Get(env("CATALOG_TIMEOUT").Parse(time.ParseDuration).Default(catalog.Timeout).Validate(httpclient.CheckTimeout))
catalog.AttemptTimeout = r.Get(env("CATALOG_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT").Parse(time.ParseDuration).Default(catalog.AttemptTimeout).Validate(httpclient.CheckAttemptTimeout))
catalog.MaxAttempts = r.Get(env("CATALOG_MAX_ATTEMPTS").Parse(strconv.Atoi).Default(catalog.MaxAttempts).Validate(httpclient.CheckMaxAttempts))
catalog.ForwardScenario = true

type clientCertificate = func(*tls.CertificateRequestInfo) (*tls.Certificate, error)

The catalog asks for a client certificate, so its URL must be https:

item.title: Init
item.description:
The cart’s settings

Everything the cart’s Init reads, in one struct:

type settings struct {
	HTTP httpserver.Settings
	Database *pgxpool.Config
	Catalog httpclient.Settings
	KeySet keySetSettings
	JWT jwt.Settings
	FaultTrustScope string
}

type keySetSettings struct {
	URL *url.URL
	Client httpclient.Settings
}

config.Struct sources and checks each one. A bad one makes Init fail, and the cart exits 78, naming its variable:

func readSettings(ctx context.Context, s *humus.Setup) (settings, error) {
	d := httpserver.DefaultSettings()
	env := func(name string) config.Value[string] { return config.Env(s.Process.Environment, name) }
	file := func(name string) config.Value[[]byte] { return env(name).Parse(readFile(s.Host.FS)) }

	read, err := config.Struct(func(r *config.Resolver) settings {
		client := httpclient.DefaultSettings()
		client.TLS = r.Get(file("JWKS_CA_FILE").Parse(certPool).Default(nil).Map(func(roots *x509.CertPool) *tls.Config {
			return &tls.Config{RootCAs: roots}
		}))
		client.Timeout = r.Get(env("JWKS_TIMEOUT").Parse(time.ParseDuration).Default(client.Timeout).Validate(httpclient.CheckTimeout))
		client.AttemptTimeout = r.Get(env("JWKS_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT").Parse(time.ParseDuration).Default(client.AttemptTimeout).Validate(httpclient.CheckAttemptTimeout))
		client.MaxAttempts = r.Get(env("JWKS_MAX_ATTEMPTS").Parse(strconv.Atoi).Default(client.MaxAttempts).Validate(httpclient.CheckMaxAttempts))

item.title: Testing
item.description:
The cart’s unit tests

The cart’s Init opens its Store and its Catalog through two functions:

func Init(ctx context.Context, s *humus.Setup) ([]humus.Service, error) {
	return initWith(ctx, s, openPostgres, openCatalog)
}

type openStore func(ctx context.Context, s *humus.Setup, cfg *pgxpool.Config) (store endpoint.Store, ping func(context.Context) error, err error)

type newCatalog func(s *humus.Setup, settings httpclient.Settings) (catalog endpoint.Catalog, ready func(context.Context) error, err error)

So its unit tests give it a Store in memory and a fake catalog, which answers from a price list, or fails when the test says so:

item.title: Deploying
item.description:
The image

One image holds the cart, the catalog and migrate, each built static, onto a distroless, non-root base:

FROM docker.io/library/golang:1.27.2-trixie@sha256:47667934874913a449b96faa7ef4777fa285d9ec29126ee80ed61c45b7cccf0e AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
COPY example/shoppingcart/go.mod example/shoppingcart/go.sum example/shoppingcart/
RUN go -C example/shoppingcart mod download
COPY . .
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go -C example/shoppingcart build -trimpath -ldflags=-s -o /out/cart . && \
 CGO_ENABLED=0 go -C example/shoppingcart build -trimpath -ldflags=-s -o /out/catalog ./catalog && \
 CGO_ENABLED=0 go -C example/shoppingcart build -trimpath -ldflags=-s -o /out/migrate ./cmd/migrate

FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian13:nonroot@sha256:e2e927ec666bae08560abb3c55d0659eceabb657f56b6782ab500a9fc7f555e3
COPY --from=build /out/cart /cart
COPY --from=build /out/catalog /catalog
COPY --from=build /out/migrate /migrate
USER 65532:65532

Build it from the repository’s root, since the module replaces humus with its directory:

item.title: Observing
item.description:
Opening Grafana

up.sh generates Grafana’s admin password into the grafana-admin Secret. Read it, then forward Grafana’s port:

kubectl --context kind-kind --namespace shoppingcart get secret grafana-admin \
 --output jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 --decode
kubectl --context kind-kind --namespace shoppingcart port-forward service/grafana 3000:3000

Sign in at http://localhost:3000 as admin.

An add’s trace

Add an item to a cart, as Deploying shows. Each server span is named after its method and /, the pattern the API is served under, so in Explore, with Tempo, find the adds by their path:

item.title: Production-ready
item.description:
The cart and the catalog meet each item. Check your own API against them:

Item How Where
Every setting sourced and checked; a bad one exits 78, naming its variable config.Struct and the packages’ checks, in the cart, the catalog and migrate The cart’s settings, The other checks, migrate’s settings
No secret in the environment, the logs or the spans the database URLs and the keys are files, read through s.Host.FS. No token is recorded, which a test of the App checks The secrets, as files, Their log records
Certificates renewed without a restart internal/certfile, on the kubernetes.io/tls Secrets that cert-manager renews. Its unit tests rewrite the files under a running server The certificates, read again when renewed
Two replicas of each service a PodDisruptionBudget of minAvailable: 1, and a rolling update of maxUnavailable: 0 The Deployments, The disruption budgets
Ready only once it has reached its dependencies, and still ready through their outages the latching monitors, on PostgreSQL and on the catalog’s readiness Readiness, The catalog’s probes, The cart’s readiness
A rollout loses no request httpserver.Main’s 5s drain, in both services, and a terminationGracePeriodSeconds above the drain, the grace period and the telemetry’s shutdown The drain
The schema is current before the code that needs it serves the migrate init container, under tern’s lock, with backwards-compatible migrations The migrations, The job, The init container
Least privilege the services’ roles read and write their tables and change no schema. A non-root, read-only container. No service account token mounted The grant, The roles, The Deployments
A caller sees only their own carts the owner, from the token’s subject, and a 404 for anyone else A cart’s owner
Prices can’t be set by a client the cart asks the catalog for each price, over mTLS. Only a token with catalog:write changes one The bodies, mTLS, The operations
Observable traces across both services, logs and metrics over OTLP, the alerts in deploy/alerts.yaml, deploy/dashboard.json, and alerts on each Deployment from the Collector’s Kubernetes cluster receiver Observing
Failures say why a 503 for a dependency that is down, a 422 for an unknown product, and problem details throughout The answers, The catalog’s answers
Failures are rehearsed the failure injection cases, in CI, and against an end user’s staging through its own Target The shared cases, The failure injection cases
Safe by default FAULT_TRUST_SCOPE empty, so no scenario is trusted. The OpenAPI document is the only open path besides the probes TrustScenario, Requiring it
